clue.text: Heard of clear spring in vale

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word for clear as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: clear weather is fair
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A traveller has been told about a clear spring somewhere in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' looks like a valley, but here it is the Latin word of leave-taking.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale is Latin for goodbye, used in English as a formal parting word, a synonym.

clue.text: Yellow flag

definitions.meaning: to yellow is to ..., as old paper does
to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.definitionFit: Fade means both to lose colour, as yellowing paper does, and to grow weaker.

clue.text: Note on morning papers

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A memo is left on top of the morning newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, nominally 500 sheets.

clue.text: This contains the complete works of Hunter

definitions.text: This contains the complete works of Hunter

parts.words: This contains the complete works of Hunter
parts.note: reads like a box set of an author named Hunter, but a hunter is a watch with a cover and its works are the movement

explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch, and its case holds the whole mechanism.

clue.text: Initially lock gold vessel in poet's office

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of lock

parts.note: aureate means golden
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone locks a golden cup away in the office of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: AUREATE is a literary word for golden.
explanation.definitionFit: The laureateship is the position held by the Poet Laureate, an official post.

clue.text: Dislike tile colour

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the colour of a roof tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tile' is jocular slang for a hat, not something on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is intense dislike, a straightforward synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Monetary unit in the market place

definitions.meaning: a small coin of Israel, one hundredth of a shekel
the public square and market of an ancient Greek city

explanation.definitionFit: Agora names both an Israeli coin and the assembly and market square of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Start again in the case of law that's restricting tax

parts.note: re means concerning, in the case of
an act is a law passed by Parliament

indicators.note: restricting says the abbreviation for that is holds the tax inside it

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Proceedings resume in a case about a law limiting taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated IE, which goes round VAT, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To reactivate something is to set it going again, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Anxious, having had locks removed?

definitions.meaning: dis- undoes a state, so with tresses undone a head is jokingly without its locks of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means worried, and jokingly split as dis-tressed it means stripped of tresses of hair.

clue.text: Girl finally discharged, so in the pink?

indicators.note: the girl's final letter is sent away, cut from the end of her name

parts.note: Diana is a girl's name
so and thus both mean therefore

explanation.surface: A girl leaves hospital at last, presumably in the pink of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' suggests good health; the question mark flags that the pink is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are garden flowers of the genus Dianthus, so the botanical name describes the pink.

clue.text: Soldiers restricted by service in the mess

indicators.note: the soldiers are hemmed in, placed inside the word for a church service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are confined to an army mess hall during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining hall but means a muddle or bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a swamp, and figuratively a confused mess one cannot escape.

clue.text: Honest, then crooked? It's looking like the brig!

parts.note: square means fair and honest
rigged means fixed dishonestly

explanation.surface: An honest sailor turns crook aboard a brig.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig carries square sails, so a square-rigged ship resembles one.

clue.text: Back in a plane, say, that's hot inside — pity

indicators.note: inside says the letter for hot goes within the word for the plane

parts.note: a plane is an example of a tree
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
quarter is mercy shown to a beaten enemy

explanation.surface: A passenger in the back of an aircraft complains it is a shame the cabin is so hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not an aircraft. A THREE-QUARTER is a back in rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the three-quarters are backs, positioned behind the halfbacks.

clue.text: Means of securing devotion

definitions.meaning: a fastening or fitting that holds something in place

explanation.definitionFit: Attachment means both a fixing device and emotional affection.

clue.text: Employee bound to contribute to turnover

parts.note: a hand is a worker
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: A worker is obliged to help the company's turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue; it is a gymnast's flip.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is an acrobatic flip over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Jewelled band Portia rarely used inside

indicators.note: the letters needed are tucked within the words Portia rarely

explanation.surface: Portia seldom wears her jewelled headband indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Source of drink found by bird where the roof sticks out

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
the eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: A bird finds water dripping from the overhang of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Infused leaves are what a cup of tea is brewed from, so they are its source.

clue.text: Veto being involved with a vice, recalling the past

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of veto and a vice are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ban is caught up with a vice, harking back to old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up memories, bringing the past to mind.

clue.text: One likely to have letters to his name

definitions.text: One likely to have letters to his name

parts.words: One likely to have letters to his name
parts.note: letters after one's name are qualifications, but here letters are post sent to someone by name

explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is sent to is the one whose name it bears.

clue.text: Unconventional route needs remaking

indicators.note: the letters of route must be made again in a new order

explanation.surface: An odd route has to be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, means eccentric or beyond normal convention.

clue.text: Type of fixer making adverse comments is two-faced

parts.note: hypo is sodium thiosulphate, the fixer used in developing photographs
critical means finding fault

explanation.surface: A fixer who is always criticising turns out to be deceitful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixer' suggests a shady operator, but it is the chemical fixer of photography, HYPO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocritical person professes one thing and does another, which is being two-faced.

clue.text: Firm paid space traveller

parts.note: Co. is short for company
met, as in met the bill, means paid

explanation.surface: A company has funded a space tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body travelling through space around the sun.

clue.text: Island's taken on a state

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England

explanation.surface: An island has taken on the status of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Extras strikers cannot claim

definitions.meaning: runs added to the score not off the bat in cricket
the batsman facing, the striker, gets no credit for these runs

explanation.definitionFit: Byes are cricket extras, run when the ball passes the bat, so not credited to the batter.

clue.text: Conundrum to resolve in game

indicators.note: resolve here means break up and reform, so the letters of in game rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzle has to be solved during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, a synonym for a conundrum.

clue.text: Plant suffering round the edge

indicators.note: round says the word for suffering wraps around the word for edge

parts.note: agony is great suffering
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A plant is wilting all around its border.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered plant of the rose family.

clue.text: Garment, needed for tense soprano's debut

parts.note: tight means taut or tense

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter of soprano

explanation.surface: A nervous singer needs the right outfit for her first performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting legwear garment covering hips, legs and feet.

clue.text: How to insert a word to get in

definitions.text: How to insert a word to get in

parts.words: How to insert a word to get in
parts.note: the idiom about struggling to contribute a word when someone talks nonstop

explanation.definitionFit: To get a word in edgeways is to manage a remark in a conversation dominated by others.
